plants.name: Camellia sasanqua
plants.description: Glossy evergreen shrubs covered in silky, open-faced blooms with golden stamens. They brighten the dim days of early winter and often drop their petals like confetti beneath the branches.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn through early winter, typically October to January
plants.location: Gardens in Japan, its native home, and the mild-winter southeastern United States
plants.funFact: Sasanqua camellias are close relatives of the tea plant, Camellia sinensis, and their seeds are pressed to make camellia oil.

plants.name: Delonix regia
plants.description: A wide, umbrella-shaped tropical tree that turns into a blaze of scarlet-orange when in full flower, with feathery fern-like leaves beneath. It lights up summer streets and parks.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to summer in the Southern Hemisphere, with main flowering often starting in late November or early December
plants.location: Tropical Queensland, Australia, including Magnetic Island
plants.funFact: Although it is one of the world's most celebrated tropical trees, it is native to Madagascar, where wild populations are now endangered.

plants.name: Helleborus niger
plants.description: A tough, low-growing perennial that opens nodding, cup-shaped white flowers with golden centers in the depths of winter. It blooms through frost and rain, when little else in the garden stirs.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early winter to spring, from about December to April
plants.location: Gardens across Europe and the cooler Northern Hemisphere, native to the mountains of central and southern Europe
plants.funFact: Its flowers often age to a rosy-pink blush, and the plant earned its festive name because it blooms around Christmas.

plants.name: Schlumbergera truncata
plants.description: A jungle cactus with arching, segmented stems that drip with vivid tubular flowers at the tips. It grows on tree branches in humid forests rather than in desert sand.
plants.location: Mountain forests of southeastern Brazil, and in homes around the world
plants.funFact: In the wild it is an epiphyte, rooting in tree crevices and moss rather than soil, and it flowers in response to shorter days and cooler nights.
